title: Fourier coefficient of a degree part
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by $\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For a function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$, let its Fourier coefficient at a multi-index $a\in\iota^n$ be its inner product with the corresponding product of basis functions. The Fourier coefficient at $a$ of the sum of all support components of $f$ indexed by subsets of size $k$ equals the coefficient of $f$ at $a$ if the number of coordinates where $a$ differs from the constant index is $k$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$\iota$ is finite, nonempty, and has decidable equality
The basis is indexed by $\iota$ and spans the real-valued functions on $\Omega$
The basis vector at the distinguished index is constant $1$
